Project Background

Renewable Energy on Navajo Nation Land

The PSH Carrizo Project proposes construction of a pumped storage hydropower (PSH) facility in the Carrizo Mountains region of the Navajo Nation in northeastern Arizona. PSH is a proven large-scale energy storage technology that uses two reservoirs at different elevations — pumping water uphill during periods of surplus energy and releasing it downhill through turbines to generate electricity on demand.

Baylor University's AVIA Lab was engaged to conduct the first aerial photogrammetric survey of both the Upper and Lower Reservoir candidate sites, providing orthomosaic imagery, digital surface models (DSMs), and high-resolution mapping data to support the feasibility assessment and environmental review of the project.

Mission Objectives

  • Execute fixed-wing UAV photogrammetry at Upper Reservoir site
  • Execute fixed-wing UAV photogrammetry at Lower Reservoir site
  • Generate orthomosaic imagery (RGB) and digital surface models
  • Assess terrain and access conditions for future survey phases
  • Engage Navajo Nation stakeholders and local partners on-site
  • Validate flight operations under Navajo Nation drone permit

Project Partners

  • Baylor University — AVIA Lab (survey team lead)
  • Navajo Nation — land access and tribal coordination
  • UES (Universal Engineering Sciences) — project proponent
  • New Mexico State University — collaborating researchers
  • Teec Nos Pos Chapter, Navajo Nation — local stakeholders
  • Quantum Systems — Trinity Pro platform support
Survey Platform

Quantum Systems Trinity Pro

The Trinity Pro is a fixed-wing VTOL (vertical take-off and landing) UAV developed by Quantum Systems GmbH. It combines the efficiency of a fixed-wing aircraft — long range and high coverage — with the flexibility of multi-rotor take-off and landing, making it ideal for remote survey sites with limited flat ground.

ManufacturerQuantum Systems GmbH
TypeFixed-wing VTOL UAV
Wingspan~2.4 m (94 in)
Max EnduranceUp to 90 min
Operating RangeUp to 40 km (VLOS)
Max Payload~600 g
CameraRGB, multispectral options
GSD at 120 m~3 cm/pixel
Launch / RecoveryVTOL — no runway needed
Flight PlanningPix4D / QGroundControl
Data ProcessingPix4Dmapper (photogrammetry)

Field Operations

Three-Day Survey Campaign

The survey team traveled from Baylor University to the Farmington, New Mexico area, then proceeded into the Navajo Nation to access both candidate reservoir sites. The mission required 4WD vehicles, satellite communication, and coordination with Navajo Nation officials and local chapter stakeholders.

Day 1 — September 11, 2026

Farmington Test Flight

Team arrived in Farmington, NM for an initial stakeholder meeting and conducted a test flight with the Trinity Pro to validate equipment and flight systems prior to entering the Navajo Nation survey area.

Day 2 — September 12, 2026

Upper Reservoir Survey

The team drove deep into the Navajo Nation via rough 4WD access roads, reaching the Upper Reservoir candidate site at elevation. The Trinity Pro executed its planned survey grid, capturing full coverage imagery of the site. Navajo Nation stakeholders and project partners joined on-site.

Day 3 — September 13, 2026

Lower Reservoir Survey

The team accessed the lower canyon terrain to survey the Lower Reservoir candidate site. The rugged red-sandstone landscape presented challenging terrain. Despite a vehicle recovery event, the team completed full survey coverage and conducted ground reconnaissance of the site.

Upper Reservoir — Day 2

Full Team at the Navajo Nation Survey Area

The Baylor AVIA team was joined by Navajo Nation stakeholders, UES project staff, and collaborating researchers from New Mexico State University at the Upper Reservoir survey area on September 12, 2026.

Full survey team and project stakeholders — Teec Nos Pos area, Navajo Nation, September 12, 2026. Left to right: Baylor AVIA students, Navajo Nation representatives, UES project team, and collaborating researchers.

Survey Deliverables

Photogrammetric Data Products

Imagery collected by the Trinity Pro was processed using Pix4Dmapper to generate orthomosaic maps and 3D digital surface models of both reservoir sites. These data products support terrain analysis, volume estimation, and engineering design for the PSH facility.

Orthomosaic — Upper Reservoir

Georeferenced RGB orthomosaic of the Upper Reservoir candidate site, generated from Trinity Pro survey imagery processed in Pix4Dmapper. Resolution: ~3 cm/pixel GSD.

3D Point Cloud Model — Upper Reservoir

Oblique 3D visualization of the Upper Reservoir terrain derived from photogrammetric reconstruction. Used for volumetric analysis and site engineering assessment.
